es.summary: Vacuna recombinante que estimula la inmunidad activa contra el virus de la hepatitis B.
key_points: Es una vacuna de subunidad recombinante que contiene la proteína de superficie (HBsAg).
Se administra en 3 dosis: 0, 1 y 6 meses (esquema estándar).
Contraindicada en personas con hipersensibilidad conocida a la vacuna o a sus excipientes.
Efectos adversos comunes: dolor, eritema y fiebre leve; anafilaxia es rara pero grave.
Se recomienda a recién nacidos, niños, adolescentes, adultos de alto riesgo y personal de salud.

mechanism: El HBsAg recombinante induce la producción de anticuerpos neutralizantes contra el virus.
Genera células B de memoria y respuesta de linfocitos T CD4+.
Proporciona inmunidad activa sin riesgo de infección real.
indications: Prevención primaria de hepatitis B en población general.
Personas con exposición ocupacional (personal de salud).
Contactos de casos de hepatitis B y pacientes con infección crónica (post‑exposición).
Viajeros a áreas de alta endemicidad.
contraindications: Hipersensibilidad conocida a la vacuna o a cualquiera de sus componentes (ej. aluminio).
Reacción anafiláctica previa a una dosis de HBV.
Enfermedad febrile aguda grave (posponer hasta recuperación).
adverse_effects: Dolor, enrojecimiento o hinchazón en el sitio de inyección (común).
interactions: Inmunosupresores pueden disminuir la respuesta inmunitaria a la vacuna.
No se reportan interacciones farmacológicas significativas.
nursing_care: Verificar historial de alergias y reacciones previas a vacunas.
Administrar vía intramuscular en deltoides con técnica aséptica.
Observar al paciente 15‑30 min después de la inyección; tener epinefrina a mano.
Registrar sitio, lote y hora de administración.
patient_teaching: Explicar la necesidad de completar el esquema de 3 dosis para inmunidad plena.
Informar que el dolor local es normal y que la fiebre leve suele resolverse en 24‑48 h.
Indicar que debe evitar frotar o masajear el sitio de inyección.
Orientar a buscar atención inmediata si aparecen urticaria, dificultad para respirar o mareos.
antidote_overdose: No hay antídoto específico; tratar reacciones alérgicas graves con epinefrina intramuscular, oxígeno y soporte vital.

related_to: hipersensibilidad a componentes de la vacuna
historia de anafilaxia a vacunas previas
outcomes: Sin signos de reacción alérgica: ausencia de urticaria, edema o dificultad respiratoria en 30 min.
Estabilidad hemodinámica: presión arterial y frecuencia cardíaca dentro de rangos normales durante observación.

interventions.action: Revisar historial de alergias y reacciones previas antes de la administración.
interventions.rationale: Identifica pacientes con mayor riesgo de reacción alérgica.

interventions.action: Mantener epinefrina 0.3 mg/ml disponible y lista para uso inmediato.
Observar al paciente 15‑30 min post‑vacunación, monitorizando signos vitales.
Enseñar al paciente y familia los signos de reacción alérgica y cuándo buscar ayuda.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la detección precoz fuera del entorno clínico.

interventions.action: Documentar lote, sitio de inyección y cualquier reacción observada.
interventions.rationale: Garantiza trazabilidad y seguimiento de eventos adversos.

en.summary: Recombinant vaccine that stimulates active immunity against the hepatitis B virus.
key_points: It is a recombinant subunit vaccine containing the surface protein (HBsAg).
It is administered in 3 doses: 0, 1, and 6 months (standard schedule).
Contraindicated in persons with known hypersensitivity to the vaccine or its excipients.
Common adverse effects: pain, erythema, and mild fever; anaphylaxis is rare but serious.
Recommended for newborns, children, adolescents, high‑risk adults, and health‑care personnel.

mechanism: Recombinant HBsAg induces production of neutralizing antibodies against the virus.
It generates memory B cells and CD4+ T‑cell responses.
Provides active immunity without risk of real infection.
indications: Primary prevention of hepatitis B in the general population.
Contacts of hepatitis B cases and patients with chronic infection (post‑exposure).
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to the vaccine or any of its components (e.g., aluminum).
Previous anaphylactic reaction to an HBV dose.
Severe acute febrile illness (delay until recovery).
adverse_effects: Pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site (common).
interactions: Immunosuppressants may reduce the immune response to the vaccine.
nursing_care: Verify allergy history and prior vaccine reactions.
Administer intramuscularly into the deltoid with aseptic technique.
Observe the patient 15‑30 min after injection; have epinephrine ready.
Document site, lot, and time of administration.
patient_teaching: Explain the need to complete the 3‑dose series for full immunity.
Inform that local pain is normal and mild fever usually resolves in 24‑48 h.
Advise against rubbing or massaging the injection site.
Instruct to seek immediate care if hives, breathing difficulty, or dizziness occur.
antidote_overdose: No specific antidote; treat severe allergic reactions with intramuscular epinephrine, oxygen, and supportive care.

related_to: history of anaphylaxis to prior vaccines
outcomes: No signs of allergic reaction: absence of hives, edema, or respiratory difficulty within 30 min.
Hemodynamic stability: blood pressure and heart rate within normal ranges during observation.

interventions.action: Review allergy history and prior reactions before administration.
interventions.rationale: Identifies patients at higher risk of allergic reaction.

interventions.action: Keep 0.3 mg/mL epinephrine available and ready for immediate use.
Observe the patient 15‑30 min post‑vaccination, monitoring vital signs.
Teach the patient and family the signs of allergic reaction and when to seek help.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates early detection outside the clinical setting.

interventions.action: Document lot, injection site, and any observed reaction.
interventions.rationale: Ensures traceability and monitoring of adverse events.

summary.0.quote: Examples of subunit, recombinant, and conjugate vaccines include the hepatitis B vaccine, human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine, and some meningococcal vaccines.

key_points.1.quote: Teens and adults (ages 15–45 years): 3 doses (0.5 mL each) intramuscularly at 0, 2, and 6 months.

key_points.2.quote: Contraindications to vaccines include hypersensitivity to the vaccine or any of its constituents.

key_points.4.quote: Vaccination is available and is recommended for children as part of the standard vaccination schedule (one dose at birth and the second by 18 months of age) and for adults at greater risk (e.g., those with certain diseases, IV-drug users, those who have sex with multiple partners).

sections.mechanism.2.quote: Through immunizations, clients build immunity without experiencing the full-blown disease, which reduces the risk of infection and contributes to public health by controlling the spread of disease.

sections.indications.1.quote: Health-care agencies are required to offer the hepatitis B vaccine to all workers who have occupational exposure to blood or other infectious materials.

sections.indications.3.quote: Vaccine is available and recommended for all children and high-risk groups (e.g., traveling to high risk area, food service workers, gay men, IV-drug users).

sections.contraindications.0.quote: Contraindications to vaccines include hypersensitivity to the vaccine or any of its constituents.

sections.adverse_effects.0.quote: Local reactions including tenderness, erythema, induration, and swelling at injection site.

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: Discuss their medical history with the health care provider and discuss the vaccine prior to immunization.
